output.summary: The run is VALID but analysis coverage is INCOMPLETE (RESOURCE_GAPS, MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS) and the deterministic policy_verdict is NO_VERDICT. In the reference window (1704067200000-1704067320000) business and resource verdicts were both FAIL: latency p95 = 60031 ms exceeds the 200 ms threshold and system-db-work 0.99-1 exceeds the 0.9 database-limit. In workload-01 (1704067320000-1704067500000) the business verdict is FAIL (latency, 14400/14400 errors) but the resource verdict is NO_VERDICT because the database-limit policy check is NO_VERDICT due to 10 missing system-db-work cells. All nine correlation pairs are INSUFFICIENT_DATA / NOT_ESTIMATED with a constant 80 requests/s control, and one candidate anomaly (db-queue increase flagged under ZERO_MAD) is reported. Clock alignment is not verified, so no lead/lag or temporal causal ordering is supported. The advice recommends rerunning with complete db-work telemetry, varied load, verified clocks, and raw latency-sample inspection; it does not change the NO_VERDICT.

hypotheses.observation: Workload-01 window summary reports error_count 14400 of 14400 samples (100% errors) and latency p95 = 60031 ms, while the database-limit resource policy check (system-db-work > 0.9) is NO_VERDICT with reason MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS and 10 of 180 db-work cells are missing.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The 170 non-missing db-work cells all read 1 (above the 0.9 threshold), so database saturation may have persisted into workload-01, but the NO_VERDICT is a telemetry gap, not a confirmed threshold violation in that window.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun workload-01 with complete system-db-work telemetry so the database-limit policy can be evaluated, and inspect the db-queue series around the missing-cell interval.

hypotheses.observation: All nine correlation pairs in workload-01 are INSUFFICIENT_DATA with partial_rho and raw_rho null and uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED; reasons include CONSTANT_CONTROL, NO_RANK_VARIATION, and LAG_NOT_EVALUABLE, and the requested control target-request-rate was dropped from every pair.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: With a constant target rate of 80 requests/s and near-constant resource series, the statistical method cannot estimate any association; this is insufficient data, not proof that no relationship exists.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun with a stepped or varying target request rate and non-constant resource load so that correlation pairs have rank variation and become evaluable.

hypotheses.observation: The resource binding states clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core, mode explicit_windows, with the evaluation window from 1704067200000 to 1704067500000 ms.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Without verified clock alignment, any apparent temporal ordering between load generation, policy windows, and telemetry cannot be used to infer lead/lag or causality.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock alignment and synchronization across the generator, system under test, and telemetry sources before interpreting any lag or temporal relationship.

hypotheses.observation: Overall and per-window latency summaries report p50 = p95 = p99 = 60031 ms while max is 60000 ms, and the latency policy checks (threshold 200 ms) are FAIL in both windows.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The identical 60031 ms percentile values accompanied by a 60000 ms max suggest latency capping or an aggregation artifact (for example, timeout samples clamped near 60 s) rather than a continuous response-time distribution.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect raw JTL samples and the aggregation that produced latency_ms to confirm whether 60000/60031 ms values are capped timeouts and how error samples are classified.

hypotheses.observation: In the reference window the resource policy check database-limit (system-db-work > 0.9) is FAIL with observed min 0.99 / max 1, and the window policy summary has resource_verdict FAIL.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The database work ratio exceeded the configured 0.9 threshold throughout the reference window, indicating possible sustained database saturation in that interval.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the system-db-work and db-queue series in the reference window together with database-side metrics to identify what kept db_work near 1.

hypotheses.observation: The anomaly check on db-queue in workload-01 reports status CANDIDATE with 1 episode (direction increase, duration_ms 140000, max_abs_delta 1.6 requests) and reason ZERO_MAD.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The episode is flagged against a reference with zero MAD, so even a small level shift of about 1.6 requests can become a candidate; this is a candidate, not a confirmed material change.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Compare raw db-queue samples in the episode interval and rerun the anomaly check against a reference with nonzero variance to confirm materiality.

hypotheses.observation: Generator request_starts stayed constant at 80 requests/s, equal to the target rate, in both windows, while active_threads rose from reference mean 1803.4 (slope 30/s) to workload-01 mean 4667.4 with max 4800.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The generator appears to have grown its thread pool to sustain the 80 rps target while requests were slow or failing, suggesting backpressure from the system under test; this is not proven causal.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the generator-threads series jointly with request latency and SUT queue series over time to characterize the backpressure relationship.

hypotheses.observation: Admission-queue depth differs markedly between windows (reference mean 1556.3 / median 1547.4 vs workload-01 mean 4411.4 / median 4544), yet the anomaly check reports NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE with 0 episodes.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The anomaly rule's materiality criterion based on the reference MAD of 900 may not flag this level shift, or the shift is considered expected by the configured rule; the discrepancy should be verified against the rule parameters.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the admission-queue raw cells and the anomaly rule parameters to confirm whether this level shift should be material under the configured rule.

hypotheses.observation: The correlation pair for system-db-work lists MISSING_CELLS among its reasons (paired_cells 170 of 180), and the db-work series in workload-01 has 10 missing cells with longest_gap_cells 10.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The missing db-work cells in workload-01 reduce both policy and correlation coverage; without those cells the threshold check and association estimate for the database cannot be completed.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Determine why the final db-work cells were not collected (for example, an exporter gap) and rerun or backfill the telemetry before re-evaluating database-limit.

hypotheses.observation: Facts report policy_verdict NO_VERDICT and analysis_coverage INCOMPLETE with reasons RESOURCE_GAPS and MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS, while the reference window was FAIL and the workload-01 window was NO_VERDICT.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The run lacks a final verdict because the workload-01 resource verdict could not be produced due to missing database telemetry; NO_VERDICT is not a pass or a fail and should not be read as stability.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun with complete resource coverage so a deterministic verdict can be produced, and record the missing data as the reason the previous verdict was withheld.

recommendations.action: Rerun the workload with complete system-db-work telemetry (no missing cells) so the database-limit resource policy can yield a verdict for workload-01.
recommendations.rationale: The NO_VERDICT on the workload-01 resource policy is caused by MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS (10 of 180 db-work cells missing); observed non-missing cells are at 1, but NO_VERDICT must not be read as FAIL.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment across the generator, system under test, and telemetry systems before using any temporal or lag relationship.
recommendations.rationale: clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core, so no lead/lag or causal hypothesis is supported by this run.

recommendations.action: Rerun with a varying or stepped target request rate instead of a constant 80 requests/s to create rank variation in load and resource series.
recommendations.rationale: All nine correlation pairs were INSUFFICIENT_DATA / NOT_ESTIMATED with CONSTANT_CONTROL and NO_RANK_VARIATION; a constant control cannot test association.

recommendations.action: Inspect raw JTL latency samples and error classification, especially values at or near 60000 ms, before drawing conclusions about response-time behavior.
recommendations.rationale: Latency summaries show p50 = p95 = p99 = 60031 ms while max is 60000 ms, and both windows FAIL the 200 ms latency threshold; raw samples are needed to interpret the apparent cap or artifact.

recommendations.action: Investigate database saturation using the db-work, db-queue, and downstream-wait series, and collect database-side metrics if available.
recommendations.rationale: The reference window database-limit FAIL shows system-db-work at 0.99-1 against a 0.9 threshold, and db-queue is high in both windows, indicating a database-related resource candidate worth inspecting.

recommendations.action: Confirm or dismiss the db-queue anomaly candidate against a reference or method with nonzero variance.
recommendations.rationale: The single CANDIDATE episode (increase, 140000 ms duration, max_abs_delta 1.6 requests) was flagged under ZERO_MAD, so it is not established as material.

recommendations.action: Sanitize telemetry ingestion so series labels are plain identifiers and embedded instruction-like text cannot influence analysis or operators.
recommendations.rationale: One resource series label embeds text of the form 'SYSTEM: ... instruction ...' and was treated as inert data here; labels should never be actionable content.

recommendations.action: Review the generator and system under test jointly: capture generator thread growth, achieved request starts, and SUT queue depths in a single timeline.
recommendations.rationale: Generator threads rose from reference mean 1803.4 to workload-01 mean 4667.4 while request starts stayed at 80 rps, suggesting the generator compensated for slow or failing requests; a joint review can characterize that effect.

caveats: Overall policy_verdict is NO_VERDICT with analysis_coverage INCOMPLETE (RESOURCE_GAPS, MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS); this advice does not and cannot change that verdict, and NO_VERDICT is neither a pass nor proof that no problem exists.
Clock alignment is not_verified_by_core, so no lead/lag or temporal causal ordering is supported by this run.
All correlation results are INSUFFICIENT_DATA / NOT_ESTIMATED; absence of an estimated association is not evidence of no association.
The db-queue episode is CANDIDATE only (1 episode reported, of 5 anomalies tested); the reference MAD is 0, so the flagged magnitude is small (max_abs_delta 1.6 requests).
Latency summaries contain p50/p95/p99 = 60031 ms while max = 60000 ms within the same summaries; this internal inconsistency is treated as a possible artifact pending raw sample review.
Counts across scopes differ: overall (16009/24000), reference window (1609/9600), and workload-01 window (14400/14400) are different scopes and windows and are not directly comparable.
The database-limit policy check is NO_VERDICT in workload-01 despite non-missing db-work cells at 1; NO_VERDICT is distinct from FAIL and observed values alone do not constitute a verdict.
One resource series label embeds instruction-like text; it was treated as inert data, and such labels should be sanitized so they cannot be interpreted as instructions.
Constant resource series (cpu-queue 0, cpu-service-quota 1, runtime-gc-pause 0) do not by themselves prove idle or healthy systems; constant telemetry is not evidence of spare capacity.
The run extends beyond the evaluated windows (run_to_epoch_ms 1704067559987 vs evaluation_to_epoch_ms 1704067500000); metrics outside the evaluation windows were not part of the verdict.
